sentences.text: Solicitor Daniel Okafor attended with client Aisha Rahman and trainee Sophie Grant.
The purpose of the meeting was to obtain the client's account of her employment at Northgate Logistics, discuss her objectives, and outline next steps.
The client worked for Northgate Logistics Limited, a warehouse off the ring road with blue cladding.
She started work on the fifth of March twenty eighteen.
She started as a picker and became team leader of the inbound goods team in June twenty twenty-one.
Her basic pay was twenty-nine thousand four hundred a year, with a shift allowance of about eighteen hundred a year.
She has type one diabetes since she was fourteen and uses a glucose sensor on her arm.
She disclosed her diabetes to her manager Linda Chu at the start of her employment.
Linda Chu left at the end of last year (twenty twenty-five) and was replaced by Gary Whitlock, who started on the twelfth of January.
On the second of February, Gary sent an email stating that breaks must be taken at fixed times (thirty minutes and two fifteens) and no one could leave the dock without his say-so.
The client emailed HR in March asking for an occupational health referral.
The occupational health report was dated the twenty-second of April and recommended short breaks as a reasonable adjustment.

The client has her original contract from twenty eighteen, payslips for May, June, July, and August, the dismissal letter dated the fourteenth of August, the appeal outcome letter dated the sixteenth of September, and a copy of her appeal email.
The client does not have a copy of the February break policy email, the occupational health report, the meeting notes from the investigation or disciplinary meetings, or the first aid log.
The client has a photo of her glucose sensor reading taken by Marcus Bell.
The client has a spreadsheet recording her job applications.
The client's primary objective is for the employer to acknowledge that they were wrong to treat her like that for being ill.
Her second priority is a proper reference so she can get a job.
Compensation is secondary to the above.
She also wishes for the employer to sort out the break issue for other staff, including a colleague with epilepsy.
The solicitor advised that the client should check with Castleford Mutual for legal expenses insurance and send the policy schedule and wording.
The solicitor advised that the client should draft a timeline of events by the second of October.
The solicitor advised that the client should ask Marcus Bell if he would be willing to give a statement.
The solicitor advised that the client should ask Linda Chu if she would be happy to talk to the solicitor.
The solicitor advised that the client should not sign any documents from the employer without talking to the solicitor first.
The solicitor advised that the client should not respond to the employer directly and should send any correspondence to the solicitor.

The solicitor advised that the client should contact ACAS within three months less one day of the dismissal (the fourteenth of August), meaning the deadline is the thirteenth of November twenty twenty-six.
The solicitor advised that the client should aim to notify ACAS by the sixteenth of October.
The solicitor advised that the client should bring a claim for unfair dismissal and discrimination arising from disability.
The solicitor advised that the client should meet again on Thursday the eighth of October at ten o'clock.
By Friday the twenty-fifth, the client must email the solicitor the occupational health report, Marcus's photo of the sensor, any unpaid payslips, and the February break policy email if found.
By Monday the twenty-eighth, the client must check with Castleford Mutual for legal expenses cover and send the policy schedule and wording.
By Friday the second of October, the client must write a timeline of events.
By Monday, the trainee Sophie Grant must draft the subject access request to Northgate.
The solicitor will check the subject access request and send it out on Tuesday.
The solicitor will send a letter confirming today's advice and funding options by Tuesday the twenty-ninth.
The next meeting is scheduled for Thursday the eighth of October at ten o'clock.
